name: Native American & Indigenous Studies
summary: Native American and Indigenous Studies examines the histories, cultures, governments, and contemporary lives of Indigenous peoples. The major centers Indigenous perspectives and knowledge.
description: This major explores the histories and cultures of Native American, Alaska Native, Native Hawaiian, and other Indigenous peoples. Coursework covers tribal histories, treaties and federal Indian law, tribal sovereignty and governance, Indigenous languages, literature and art, environmental knowledge and land rights, and contemporary issues such as health, education, and economic development. Many programs offer study of an Indigenous language and partnerships with tribal nations. Graduates work for tribal governments, federal agencies such as the Bureau of Indian Affairs, museums, schools, and nonprofits, and many pursue law or graduate study.
